subject.title: Feature: Session authentication PIN gate (framework-level tool blocking)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core opt-in session PIN tool gate, and if so what trusted secret source, verifier path, and session-state reset semantics should it use?
rationale: The request changes core auth/config/session state and could create false security if PIN storage or verification is handled in prompt space or conversation history.

options.title: Sponsor a core security design
options.body: Define the opt-in secret source, trusted verifier command or internal tool, authenticated SessionEntry state, reset behavior, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep it plugin-owned
options.body: Document the before_tool_call plugin pattern and close or narrow the core request if maintainers do not want a built-in session-auth primitive.

options.title: Defer to broader auth roadmap
options.body: Leave this open but blocked until a larger gateway/operator/session auth model decides whether per-session gates belong in core.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core security design
recommendation.body: Define the opt-in secret source, trusted verifier command or internal tool, authenticated SessionEntry state, reset behavior, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the strongest overlap between the before-tool-call hook path, plugin approval behavior, and security ownership signals.
